summary: AE+SE demo of console's Trace Garden (request flow visualization), error analysis, and request-log stitching for an e-commerce use case. Customer focused on intermittent 95th pct latency spikes and occasional hallucinations during product-description augmentation. topics: KV cache cold start and fallback behavior
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-09 15:00 UTC | Duration: 56m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Chris Martinez (Redwood AE), Nadia Chen (Redwood SE), Omar Li (Redwood PM), Tara Singh (Bluebloom CTO), Mateo Ruiz (Platform), Priya Kapoor (SRE), Jamal Ortiz (Privacy)

[00:00] Chris Martinez: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i think we have about 55 minutes, we'll walk through the Trace Garden console and then leave time for Q&A. um Tara, you mentioned in the notes some intermittent latency spikes at the 95th percentile?
[00:18] Tara Singh: yeah thanks chris. that's right. we've got a production service that augments product descriptions during checkout. most requests are fine, but like 2-3% see 300-600ms extra latency and occasionally the model hallucinates a nonexistent color.
[00:33] Mateo Ruiz: sorry to interrupt, just to add, those spikes correlate with higher cart sizes, so the prompt length changes and maybe KV cache behavior?
[00:42] Nadia Chen: that's useful context. we're gonna show how Trace Garden surfaces request timeline, model variant fallbacks, and KV cache hits/misses. you'll see the trace map and the raw request logs stitched together.
[00:56] Omar Li: quick FYI — we'll reference the pilot template later, but no pressure.
[01:02] Priya Kapoor: also we need to confirm encryption at rest and KMS integration.
[01:09] Chris Martinez: totally, Jamal from privacy is here too. we'll show audit logs and where you can find them in the console. ok nadia, over to you.

[01:22] Nadia Chen: demo mode. navigating to the Trust + Observability > Trace Garden. first panel is a heatmap of requests over time. you can click a spike and it opens a request waterfall. here's an example from your anonymized sample: request id bb-req-20260601-7c9.
[01:40] (screen share noise)
[01:46] Nadia Chen: the waterfall shows client ingress -> routing -> model router -> inference runtime -> post-process. each segment has latency and token counts. see how the KV cache step here is annotated as "KV catch miss" — apologies the auto-transcript sometimes says catch instead of cache — but you can see a miss caused an extra 120ms while KV warmed.
[02:12] Mateo Ruiz: ah that's the miss we suspected. can you filter for similar requests?
[02:16] Nadia Chen: yep, use the filter on the left for the prompt hash or endpoint. applying that shows a cluster of misses aligned to cart size > 7 items.
[02:27] [02:27] Tara Singh: is that because of sequence length or because KV shard affinity changed?
[02:34] Nadia Chen: good question. the trace shows the model router bounced to a quantized variant when throughput spiked. that variant has smaller KV shard affinity causing cold lookup.
[02:45] Chris Martinez: so there's a routing policy tradeoff — we can prioritize latency by pinning to a dedicated variant, or prioritize cost by routing to a cheaper quantized model.
[02:55] Priya Kapoor: what about fallback behavior when a variant OOMs or errors? we saw one instance where responses returned with an empty field rather than an explicit error.
[03:05] Nadia Chen: you can configure automatic fallback rules. in this trace the runtime attempted incremental fallback to a slightly smaller context model, but post-processing swallowed an empty payload. the Trace Garden highlights the mismatch and links to the raw request log.
[03:17] Jamal Ortiz: for privacy, where are those raw logs stored and how long do they persist?
[03:23] Chris Martinez: retention is configurable per project; hosted defaults to 30 days but you can change retention and enable log redaction. for Private deployments you own the storage and can tie into your KMS/HSM for keys.
[03:36] Tara Singh: does that mean if we do dedicated it's still hosted, or fully customer-managed?
[03:42] Omar Li: Dedicated is reserved capacity in our infra — your data still flows through Redwood control plane but we provide isolation and SLA. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you customer-managed control plane and storage if you need air-gap.
[03:55] Mateo Ruiz: hmm we have strict EU residency and a bunch of compliance hoops, so Private might be preferred but budget is a factor.
[04:02] Chris Martinez: that's why the pilot proposal includes both a hosted POC and an optional Private connector for a short-term residency check.

[04:15] [04:15] Nadia Chen: picking up on the trace, i'll jump to the raw logs inspector. it stitches request metadata, model debug headers (e.g., active_kv_shard, token_cache_hits), and postprocess errors. notice this error line: "postproc: missing sku field -> sanitized output sent". that's the hallucination symptom — the model omitted expected attribute.
[04:40] Tara Singh: that matches tickets we've seen. any quick mitigations? temperature? prompt clamp?
[04:45] Nadia Chen: yes common immediate mitigations — lower sampling temperature, add strict schema constraints via function calling/structured output, and enable a defensive post-process which checks required fields and falls back to a deterministic rewrite.
[04:58] Priya Kapoor: will lowering temp increase latency? we care about 95th pct.
[05:03] Nadia Chen: negligible effect on compute; larger impact is on quality, sometimes you need more tokens to be explicit. the cost tradeoff is often small.

[05:15] Chris Martinez: quick aside — you mentioned hallucinations coinciding with longer prompts. our Optimize tool can recommend quantization or kernel profiles that keep latency stable across variable sequence lengths. we'll demo a suggestion rule later.

[05:30] [05:30] Nadia Chen: switching to the timeline view, you can replay the request timeline. pressing playback highlights events and correlates with infra metrics (GPU load, queue depth). see here at 14:22 UTC the queue depth spiked and routing retried a different host. that retrial added ~200ms.
[05:51] Mateo Ruiz: is that because autoscaling was slow?
[05:54] Nadia Chen: in this case autoscaler took ~18s to bring an extra worker, routing retried in the interim. tuning the scaler policy to be more aggressive or enabling burst pools mitigates this.
[06:06] Tara Singh: we run k8s-based inference in-house for some things — could Redwood's autoscaler integrate with our metrics?
[06:12] Omar Li: yes for Private we can plug into your cluster metrics, and for Dedicated we expose hooks and webhooks you can use to influence autoscaling behavior.

[06:25] [06:25] Chris Martinez: let's talk about cost. if we pin to a dedicated variant to eliminate routing jitter, we reduce latency but increase cost. any budget constraints we should know about?
[06:36] Tara Singh: we're targeting at most a 10% increase in infra spend for a significant latency improvement. if the pilot can show 95th pct latency cut in half, that's worth it.
[06:47] Nadia Chen: ok noted. we'll include cost projections in the pilot doc — token cost + reserved capacity math.

[07:00] [07:00] Mateo Ruiz: back to logs — can we export redactable logs to our S3? we need to ingest into Splunk.
[07:07] Chris Martinez: yes, exports to your S3 or SIEM are supported; we support JSONL with PII redaction hooks.
[07:14] Jamal Ortiz: and SAML SSO + RBAC? we need audit trails mapped to our users.
[07:19] Omar Li: SAML, OIDC, fine-grained RBAC, and long-term audit log retention are available in Enterprise/Private plans.

[07:28] [07:28] Nadia Chen: demo — now toggling into error analysis mode. Trace Garden groups similar error signatures across routes. here's a cluster of "empty payload" cases; clicking into the cluster shows the canonical failing prompt, last successful token, and the model's debug headers.
[07:45] Tara Singh: is the debug header instrumentation added automatically? how invasive is it?
[07:49] Nadia Chen: minimal footprint — we emit lightweight debug headers from the runtime and stitch them with the request metadata. for Private you can adjust verbosity.

[08:02] [08:02] Chris Martinez: quick question from Mateo, are you already using any LLM provider in prod?
[08:07] Mateo Ruiz: yeah we have a hybrid setup — some calls to Vertex for classification, and OpenAI for chat features. we're evaluating a consolidated path.
[08:14] Chris Martinez: ok good to know. we often see customers want a single inference plane. we can emulate your current models during pilot so you can compare.

[08:28] [08:28] Nadia Chen: showing the request log stitching: each trace links to 1) raw request payload, 2) model variant used, 3) kernel profile, 4) any fallback events, 5) postprocess diffs. you can download a zipped artifact for forensic analysis.
[08:44] Priya Kapoor: can the trace annotate external API calls within postprocess (e.g., our pricing service)?
[08:49] Nadia Chen: yes if you instrument the outbound call in your app with the request id, Trace Garden will stitch it. we also support auto-correlation via headers.

[09:01] [09:01] Tara Singh: what about KV cache warmup strategies? can we pre-warm keys for expected cart combos?
[09:07] Nadia Chen: absolutely — Optimize has a pre-warm job you can schedule based on traffic patterns. also you can set longer TTLs for hot keys. we'll include a pre-warm run in the pilot scope.

[09:19] [09:19] Chris Martinez: let's do a quick live repro of a failing request. Nadia will replay a redacted request you uploaded earlier.
[09:24] (short pause, keyboard noises)
[09:30] Nadia Chen: replaying bb-req-20260601-7c9. watch the waterfall — routing retry at step 3, KV miss at step 4, then postprocess sanitized the output. i'll open the raw token trace — you can see the model produced token "azure" for color instead of "navy" which caused mismatch to your SKU resolver.
[09:53] Tara Singh: yeah that's the ticket 314 we filed. how do we prevent that?
[09:57] Nadia Chen: options: a) run a deterministic postfilter that checks the color token against allowed values and map to nearest SKU, b) use function calling to enforce enumerated outputs, c) if it's latency-related, pin to a dedicated variant to avoid routing-induced token dropout.
[10:12] Mateo Ruiz: deterministic postfilter sounds safest initially.

[10:16] [10:16] Chris Martinez: time check — we're about 45 minutes in. any remaining big questions?
[10:21] Priya Kapoor: one about SLA: what uptime/latency SLOs do you offer on Dedicated?
[10:26] Omar Li: Dedicated has a 99.9% uptime SLA and latency targets that vary by model family; we'll include concrete numbers in the pilot deck.
[10:34] Jamal Ortiz: data residency confirmation?
[10:36] Chris Martinez: for Private we can host in EU region and you control storage; for Dedicated we can sign data residency to keep logs in EU region.

[10:45] [10:45] Tara Singh: last quick ask — can we run a 2-week pilot, sample 5000 requests/day, and measure 95th pct latency and hallucination rate?
[10:53] Chris Martinez: yes, that's exactly the pilot we propose. i'll follow up with a scope and pricing.

[11:00] [11:00] Nadia Chen: final tip — you'll get a Trace Garden alert when similar error clusters exceed a threshold. you can wire that into PagerDuty or Slack.
[11:08] Chris Martinez: great. recap of next steps: chris sends pricing/pilot scope/security docs; nadia runs KV-cache repro and shares logs; bluebloom uploads redacted request IDs. we aim to kick the pilot by 2026-06-20.
[11:27] Tara Singh: sounds good, appreciate the deep dive.
[11:31] Mateo Ruiz: thanks everyone.
[11:33] Chris Martinez: thanks all, we'll follow up. bye.

End of transcript.

References shared during call: Pilot proposal doc (link: https://redwood.example/pilot/BB-4421), Security whitepaper (link: https://redwood.example/security/soc2.pdf), KV-cache repro template (link: https://redwood.example/ops/kv-repro.xlsx)
questions: Can Redwood pin a dedicated model variant to reduce routing jitter?
How are raw logs retained and can they be exported to S3 with PII redaction?
Can Trace Garden stitch external service calls via request ID?
